blockers.title: news-sitemap.xml serves an empty URL set
blockers.subclass: Deliberate, founder-hardened publish barrier -- not a defect
evidence: curl of https://www.galaxysportsedge.com/news-sitemap.xml (prior session) -> <urlset ...></urlset>, zero <url> entries

Root-caused this session: apps/web/lib/journal/load.ts loadPublicJournalEntries()/loadPublicJournalEntry() (the only readers behind news-sitemap.xml, RSS, /journal, /journal/[slug]) filter strictly on ModelJournalEntry.status === "PUBLISHED"

Repo-wide grep for `modelJournalEntry` (excluding node_modules/tests) returns exactly 6 files: create (-> DRAFT), PATCH edit (DRAFT/REVIEW_PENDING only), submit (-> REVIEW_PENDING), retract (PUBLISHED -> RETRACTED only), public-guard.ts, load.ts -- none ever write status:"PUBLISHED". The pre-existing test apps/web/__tests__/cockpit-journal-route.test.ts:109 was itself titled 'wires Journal compliance scan before publish transitions exist', confirming this was a known, named gap in application code.

First attempted this as a code fix: built POST /api/cockpit/journal/[id]/publish (ADMIN-gated, REVIEW_PENDING precondition, fresh compliance re-scan of the DB-sourced body) plus an editor Publish button. `npx vitest run` from apps/web then failed the draft-only guardrail test: scripts/guardrails/draft-only.mjs FAILed with 4 hits, all in the new route file (status:"PUBLISHED" / publishedAt:new Date() inside Prisma data: blocks) -- a REQUIRED CI job (.github/workflows/ci.yml) that fails the build on ANY apps/web|components|lib|workers|packages file performing a 'publish-side write', per its own doc comment: 'the read side is the legitimate way to render a manually-published row'

git log on draft-only.mjs: hardened in commit 0e56c4770e715630eaaac974702336447e367b5a ('close scanner/CI bypasses (#119)'), a founder-authorized merge (2026-07-17) that deliberately stripped bypass-comment exemptions so no code path -- including an admin-gated one -- can carve out an exception

Same pattern independently confirmed in the parallel ContentDraft/ContentReview system (apps/web/lib/content-engine/types.ts, .../persist-draft.ts:61-62, .../review/route.ts): publishedAt is hard-pinned null and never written by any route either. Two independently-built content pipelines share the identical invariant -- application code may draft/edit/scan/review, but the PUBLISHED flip is deliberately kept outside CI-scanned application code.

Independently corroborated by gse-verifier this session (confirmed draft-only.mjs is required+deliberately hardened) before the attempted fix (route file + editor button + test file) was fully reverted -- git status --short / git diff --stat both empty, confirmed clean
blockers.impact: None on correctness/security/revenue. The empty news-sitemap.xml is the CORRECT, intended behavior of a deliberately hardened publish barrier, not a pipeline defect -- zero Model Journal entries have ever been published out-of-band, so zero should appear. SEO upside (Google News eligibility) stays unrealized until the founder publishes an entry through the intended out-of-band mechanism.
blockers.blastRadius: SEO/news-discovery surface only. No correctness/revenue/security exposure.
blockers.canonicalOwner: Founder -- publishing Model Journal content is an intentional out-of-band action, not an agent-buildable code path.
blockers.dependencies: None blocking further campaign work. Closed as intentional; does not gate LC-007/LC-008.
blockers.smallestSafeFix: N/A -- no code fix exists to make. An in-app Publish route/button would require deliberately weakening a founder-hardened CI guardrail explicitly designed to prevent exactly that, which is squarely inside this campaign's own never-auto-publish / never-open-gates-without-founder-authorization boundary.
blockers.verification: npx vitest run (apps/web) reproduces the draft-only guardrail FAIL when the publish route exists, and OK (0 hits) with it removed. Working tree confirmed clean after revert.
blockers.rollback: N/A -- no code change shipped for this finding.
blockers.reEntryCondition: OWNER_GATE. Decision: whether/how Model Journal entries should ever reach PUBLISHED. Why founder authority is required: the only path that doesn't weaken a founder-hardened CI invariant is an out-of-band action outside application code (e.g. a direct DB/Prisma Studio update on a REVIEW_PENDING row) -- or the founder could explicitly authorize a new, narrowly-scoped in-app publish mechanism with a deliberate, reviewed exemption in draft-only.mjs, but broadening that guardrail's allowlist is a founder decision, not an autonomous one. Safe non-destructive default: leave news-sitemap.xml/RSS/journal empty (current, correct state) until the founder chooses a path. Work completed around the gate: root-caused and documented the exact mechanism (this entry); no code changed. Re-entry condition: founder specifies which mechanism they want.

blockers.title: Model Journal public read-time guard missed numeric performance claims (word-list scan only)
blockers.subclass: Latent/dormant at time of discovery -- fixed proactively, not a live incident
evidence: Found by gse-red-team during the LB-006 investigation: apps/web/lib/journal/public-guard.ts's guardPublicJournalBody/guardPublicJournalTitle called scanForBannedPhrases (apps/web/lib/trust-claims.ts:446) -- a fixed banned-WORD list only. A body like 'The model closed 12-3 ATS this cycle, a 71% cover rate' contains no banned word, only numbers, so it passed the guard unredacted.

apps/web/lib/blog/public-guard.ts already solved this exact problem for Blog content (public-number-audit-2026-07-16, finding #6) by using scanPublicCopyForClaims (apps/web/lib/trust-claims.ts:624), which adds scanForNumericPerformanceClaims (ROI-of-N%, win-loss records, units-profit claims, percent-near-a-performance-word) on top of the word list -- apps/web/__tests__/blog-public-guard.test.ts already proves this exact regression is closed for Blog. The Model Journal guard was never given the same fix.

Reproduced directly: 'The model closed 12-3 ATS this cycle, a 71% cover rate, and is up +14 units on the season.' returns zero hits from scanForBannedPhrases (confirmed in apps/web/__tests__/journal-public-guard.test.ts's new test) -- proving the gap was real, not theoretical.
blockers.impact: None realized: zero ModelJournalEntry rows have ever reached PUBLISHED (see LB-006), so this guard has never actually been exercised against real content in production. This was a live gap in shipped, reachable code (not a reverted/hypothetical route) that would have let a fabricated numeric stat (CLAUDE.md rule #2: no fabricated stats) reach /journal, /journal/[slug], RSS, and news-sitemap.xml the moment any entry is ever published by whatever mechanism the founder eventually chooses (see LB-006's OWNER_GATE) -- fixed proactively, before it could matter, rather than left for whenever LB-006 is re-entered.
blockers.blastRadius: Public Model Journal surfaces only, and only once/if the founder ever publishes an entry (LB-006 is CLOSED/OWNER_GATE, zero publish path exists in application code today).
blockers.smallestSafeFix: Swap scanForBannedPhrases -> scanPublicCopyForClaims in apps/web/lib/journal/public-guard.ts (both functions return the same BannedPhraseHit[] shape; drop-in), mirroring the identical, already-proven blog-guard fix.
blockers.verification: apps/web/__tests__/journal-public-guard.test.ts: 4 new tests (numeric-claim body redacted, numeric-claim title redacted, clean unrelated-number prose still passes, fixture-contains-no-banned-word sanity check) -- all passing alongside the 5 pre-existing tests in the same file (9/9). npx tsc --noEmit and eslint --max-warnings=0 both clean. node scripts/guardrails/draft-only.mjs still OK (this is a read-time guard change, not a publish-write -- does not touch that invariant).
